At a seminar titled "Vietnam-China Businesses: Connecting Manufacturing, Logistics, and Global Value Chains" on Oct. 29, speakers called for closer economic integration beyond traditional trade. The event was part of the 2026 Autumn Economic Forum in Ho Chi Minh City.
Xu Shou, acting consul general of China in HCMC, said the two economies had complementary industrial structures and supply chains.
"Cooperation between Chinese and Vietnamese businesses has moved beyond traditional trade in goods into a new phase of supply chain coordination, technology exchange, and knowledge sharing," he said.
Chinese companies have experience in smart manufacturing, modern logistics and innovation and are ready to deepen cooperation with Vietnamese partners, Xu said. He called for stronger links between suppliers and downstream businesses, as well as collaboration in technology transfer, process management, quality control and workforce training.
China is Vietnam's largest trading partner, with bilateral trade exceeding US$256 billion in 2025. Trade reached more than $253 billion in the first nine months of 2026, up 37.6% year-on-year.
During the same period, investors from China, including Hong Kong, received licenses for 1,104 new projects in Vietnam, with registered capital of $4.5 billion, up 31.35%. China ranked fourth among Vietnam's investment partners, with manufacturing accounting for about 80.61% of registered capital.
Yang Wen Bin, acting chairman of the HCMC Chapter of the Chinese Business Association in Vietnam, said the figures reflected Vietnam's investment appeal and the potential for greater cooperation in manufacturing, logistics and supply chains.
Yang Wen Bin, Acting Chairman of the HCMC Chapter of the Chinese Business Association in Vietnam, speaks at the 2026 Autumn Economic Forum in HCMC on Oct. 29, 2026. Photo courtesy of AEF 2026
Yang urged businesses to expand cooperation in advanced manufacturing, electronics, information technology, green energy and supporting industries, alongside technology exchanges, workforce training and investment partnerships.
He said deeper integration could help Vietnamese businesses participate more extensively in regional and global production networks.
Jesse Choi, CEO of Sunwah Group in Southeast Asia and Sunwah Innovations, and chairman of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area Entrepreneurs Alliance in Vietnam, said closer manufacturing and supply chain ties could support cooperation in technology, logistics, finance and human resource development.
Sunwah established Sunwah Innovations in 2020. Its innovation spaces in HCMC, Hanoi and Da Nang connect businesses, startups, universities and investors with partners in China and other markets.
Through exchange programs, business networking and technology partnerships, the initiative helps commercialize research, connect technology solutions with domestic demand and give Vietnamese businesses access to international opportunities, Choi said.
Speakers also called for stronger road, waterway and railway connections, smart border gates, digital supply chains, information sharing and harmonized technical standards.
Xu urged both countries to pursue joint ventures in areas including urban railways, innovative trade platforms and cross-border finance to deepen their participation in global value chains.
At a meeting with a delegation from the Research Office of China's State Council on Oct. 27, Vietnamese Deputy Minister of Finance Nguyen Thi Bich Ngoc outlined five pillars for bilateral cooperation.
She called for stronger manufacturing supply chain links, technology cooperation and research and development, as well as strategic infrastructure development, particularly the Lao Cai-Hanoi-Hai Phong railway.
Ngoc also proposed closer logistics links, smart border gates and customs cooperation to reduce trade costs, and encouraged Chinese financial institutions to participate in Vietnam's international financial center.
